key_insight: The paper shows that boundary-actuated reinforcement learning can stabilize and damp vibrations in a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest beam using a reduced-order PDE model.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-driven control route for flexible structures where boundary actuation is practical and classical model-based tuning may be difficult.
method: Model the beam with a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest linear PDE under simply supported boundary conditions.
Reduce the infinite-dimensional system via eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection.
Train a PPO controller on the resulting continuous-time Markov decision process and compare it with LQR.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic numerical comparison between PPO-based control and the classical LQR regulator, with attention to vibration suppression, energy dissipation, and actuator limits.
watch_item: Performance depends on the reduced-order approximation and discretization, so stability or accuracy may degrade if the truncation misses important beam dynamics.
paper_title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
